The Windows reports write a label and a value per line, and a document
about them quotes those lines. The network report opens with a banner of
its own:

Windows IP Configuration

and names the machine on the line under it, padding the label with dots
out to the value column:

   Host Name . . . . . . . . . . . . : EXAMPLE
   Primary Dns Suffix  . . . . . . . : example.invalid

The blocks that follow it open with a heading naming the adapter, such
as

Ethernet adapter Ethernet:

The system report pads its values into a column instead and writes no
dots at all:

Host Name:                     EXAMPLE
OS Name:                       Microsoft Windows
OS Version:                    0.0.00000 N/A Build 00000

A memory figure is written rounded there, as 16,384 MB, with a
separator in the number and a unit after it.

None of these lines is output on its own; they are quoted here so that a
reader can recognise one when it arrives.
